media:group.media:title: Introducing the Garment GUI!
media:group.media:description:
A touchscreen you can wear on your sleeve! Led by Asst Prof Tural Khudiyev from NUS Materials Science and Engineering at the NUS College of Design and Engineering, the research team developed a fibre that functions as pixels and senses touch at the same time — creating the world’s first touchscreen built into a washable and breathable garment.
The technology could pave the way for clothing that serves as an interface to our health data and digital devices. Combined with AI, it could enable personalised health monitoring, feedback and assistance.

media:group.media:title: He Builds Exoskeletons
media:group.media:description:
Can exoskeletons turn us into superhumans?🦾 Not quite.
Instead, they help us perform our tasks more safely and effectively. For Assoc Prof Yu Haoyong, this mission is deeply personal. Inspired by his late father's struggles with mobility after a stroke, he and his team are developing technology that restores not just movement, but independence and quality of life.
Their key innovation? Exoskeletons that don't control users but adapt intuitively to their movement.
This technology has the potential to: • Restore lost functions in patients after a stroke or spinal cord injury • Reduce physical strain and prevent injuries in physically demanding jobs • Empower seniors to live independently
The NUS team has recently completed a trial at Tan Tock Seng Hospital to refine an exoskeleton developed to help patients regain arm movement.
Watch the full video to see the NUS team’s exoskeletons in action!

media:group.media:title: Momigo wins 2026 James Dyson Award
media:group.media:description:
Nicolette Wong, an NUS Engineering (Industrial Design) alumna from the Class of 2026 watched her older sister navigate the challenges of breastfeeding on the go as a first-time mother, and wondered: could there be a way to make the journey of new parenthood feel a little lighter?🎈That question led to Mömigo — an innovative all-in-one breast milk storage and feeding system designed to make the journey from storage to warming to feeding more seamless.
Over 10 months, Nicolette spoke with parents and lactation consultants, tested concepts, and 3D-printed prototype after prototype – listening and learning, and transforming these lessons into ideas and innovation. Her creativity and persistence eventually earned Mömigo the 2026 James Dyson Award Singapore title🏆
But the work doesn’t stop here. Nicolette is now working towards bringing Mömigo to the market, and hopes her work can contribute to bigger conversations about how we design for motherhood care as a whole. #NUSResearch #NUSImpact #NUSAlumni #NUSInnovation

entry.title: Making soft robots smarter and more reliable

media:group.media:title: Making soft robots smarter and more reliable
media:group.media:description:
Soft robots have wide-ranging applications such as in surgery, eldercare, rehabilitation, underwater exploration and environmental monitoring, thanks to their gentle, flexible bodies. But that same softness makes them hard to control. Professor Cecilia Laschi and her team at NUS Mechanical Engineering in the NUS College of Design and Engineering are developing new ways to make soft robots smarter and more reliable. #NUSResearch
Taking inspiration from the fluid, intelligent movement of the octopus, the team is translating nature's ingenuity into more adaptable robots. With AI, these robots can learn how their soft bodies behave, enabling more precise movements and safer interactions. #NUSInnovation
Prof Laschi envisions a future where soft robots are so seamlessly woven into our everyday lives that you hardly notice them, quietly making the world around us safer and smoother. #NUSImpact

entry.title: Official launch of the ST-NUS HELIX Corporate Lab

media:group.media:title: Official launch of the ST-NUS HELIX Corporate Lab
media:group.media:description: STMicroelectronics and the National University of Singapore officially launched the ST–NUS HELIX Corporate Lab on 24 August 2026. This is a four-year strategic research initiative focused on advancing the next generation of edge AI technologies. HELIX, which stands for Hardware for Embodied Low-power Intelligent Xcceleration, will enable new generative and embodied AI use cases at the edge through system-to-silicon innovation.

entry.title: Parenting vs PhDs: which is more challenging? 👶📚

media:group.media:title: Parenting vs PhDs: which is more challenging? 👶📚
media:group.media:description:
Parenting vs PhDs: which is more challenging? 👶📚
PhD graduates from the Class of #NUS2026 Mervin Tee and Cindy Chan took on both at the same time. While pursuing their PhDs at @SSHSPH, the couple welcomed their first child, balancing thesis revisions, research setbacks, sleepless nights with newborn feeds, and the joys of early parenthood.
For Mervin, who once failed his O-Levels, the journey to a PhD has been anything but conventional. He persevered through polytechnic and university while working part-time, eventually completing his PhD in record time and graduating alongside Cindy. For Cindy, earning a PhD while navigating pregnancy, childbirth and the demands of caring for a newborn was an equally remarkable achievement.
Through partnership, resilience and unwavering support for one another, Mervin and Cindy prove that life's most demanding journeys can become deeply meaningful. 👨‍🎓👩‍🎓👶

entry.title: From the Wushu Carpet to What's Next

media:group.media:title: From the Wushu Carpet to What's Next
media:group.media:description:
From training together for a decade, to representing Singapore and NUS in Wushu, to graduating today, Kimberly (Law) and Yin Shuen (Computing) have shared parallel journeys every step of the way.
For years, they balanced the demands of competitive sport with rigorous academics. They represented Singapore at the Southeast Asia Games and Asian Games, brought home for home multiple medals for NUS and Singapore at the ASEAN University Games and somehow still found time to prepare for exams, projects and competitions all at once.
Now, they're both closing a chapter in their competitive Wushu careers- but their journey with the sport is far from over.
Kimberly, who made history by winning Singapore's first Asian Games Wushu medal in 2023 , is now coaching the next generation of athletes while preparing for the Bar later this year. Yin Shuen, who clinched a bronze medal at the 2025 SEA Games, is also giving back as a youth coach while building her career in business analytics.
From national athletes to #NUS2026 graduates, and now mentors inspiring the next generation, we couldn't be prouder of all they've achieved ! 💙🧡
